newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp U.S. card losses rise more slowly.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp U.S. card losses rise more slowly.

text.p: Charge-offs in Citicorp's U.S. credit card business are rising at a slower rate, executive vice president and principal financial officer Thomas Jones told analysts Tuesday.

"It certainly looks like the increases are tailing off," he said, adding that the 6.13 loss rate in the second quarter of 1997 reported earlier Tuesday was only a marginal increase from 5.91 percent in the first quarter of 1997.

William Campbell, executive vice president and head of the consumer business, was asked about what plans Citicorp might have to fix its domestic card business. Campbell said the company was looking at several steps it might take.
"We do not believe we have done a great job yet of bundling in our card business," he said.
Bundling would involve the marketing of other Citicorp products to card customers.
On another topic, Jones observed that Citicorp had a "good" quarter in foreign exchange with trading revenue rising to $290 million from $225 million a year ago.

Jones noted that during the quarter there were unfounded rumors about Citicorp having problems amid the financial turmoil in Thailand. But he said "we tend to be fairly cautious" in its approach to trading.
